categories.title: Exploration
categories.description: Finding and ranking targets before a mine exists.

ideas.title: Survey-Bias Audit for Prospectivity Models
ideas.summary: Test whether a prospectivity map is finding geology or only echoing where people already explored.
ideas.problem: Known deposits cluster in well-explored areas and familiar deposit types, so models can reinforce old exploration habits and rank under-explored ground too low.
ideas.approach: Re-score maps with spatial sampling-bias corrections, simulate what the map would say if every area had been explored equally, and publish a bias score next to every target.
ideas.evidence: Industry talks (SMEDG, 2026) list bias toward well-explored regions as a core risk, and negative-label handling in prospectivity mapping was called a neglected area (EGU, 2024). I found no standard audit method.
ideas.start: Take one public dataset, hide the best-explored 30% of the area, and measure how the ranking of the rest shifts.

ideas.title: From Explanation to Field Test
ideas.summary: Turn a model's explanation into ranked geological hypotheses, each paired with the cheapest survey that could confirm it.
ideas.problem: Explainability tools show which data layers drove a score, but the geologist still has to decide what to do next.
ideas.approach: Map feature attributions to deposit-model hypotheses, then choose the confirming measurement (soil line, geophysical profile, one hole) with the best information per dollar.
ideas.evidence: Explainable AI is common in prospectivity research. I did not find tools that link explanations to survey design, but this needs a proper literature check.
ideas.start: Pair the SHAP output of an existing model with a small table of cost and information value per survey type.

ideas.title: Post-Mortem Learning from Failed Targets
ideas.summary: Classify why AI-ranked targets failed, and predict the likely failure mode before drilling.
ideas.problem: False positives are usually fed back only as extra training labels, so the reason for failure (cover, alteration mismatch, structure, data gap) is lost.
ideas.approach: Build a library of failed targets labelled with causes, then train a second model that flags targets at risk of each failure mode.
ideas.evidence: A 2025 district case study reports using false positives to retune its model, without analysing their causes (IIMP, WMC proceedings).
ideas.start: Review 20 failed targets from one district and tag each with a simple cause list.

sources.label: IIMP, AI and Data-Driven Decision Making

categories.title: Resource & Planning
categories.description: Turning drill data into resource models and mine plans.

ideas.title: Core-Loss Uncertainty in Resource Models
ideas.summary: Carry the effect of lost core into grade and density uncertainty instead of ignoring it.
ideas.problem: Poor core recovery biases grades, yet resource models usually treat the recovered sample as representative.
ideas.approach: Learn how recovery relates to rock type and drilling parameters, then propagate it as extra uncertainty or a bias correction in estimation.
ideas.evidence: 2026 work uses machine learning to adapt drilling parameters and reduce core loss. I did not find work on propagating the remaining loss into resource models.
ideas.start: On one project, compare grades from high- and low-recovery intervals within the same domain.

sources.label: Adaptive control of drilling to reduce core loss, 2026

ideas.title: Reconciliation-Driven Model Correction
ideas.summary: Use years of model-versus-mill reconciliation to find where a resource model is systematically wrong.
ideas.problem: Reconciliation factors are reported as site-wide numbers, which hides spatial and domain-specific bias.
ideas.approach: Train a model on reconciliation residuals by domain, depth and rock type, and use it to adjust short-term plans with stated uncertainty.
ideas.evidence: Machine-learning grade control is well studied (for example Carmen de Andacollo, 2020). I did not confirm work built on reconciliation history.
ideas.start: Plot monthly reconciliation errors by block and domain.

ideas.title: Scenario Agent for Life-of-Mine Plans
ideas.summary: An agent that generates and stress-tests alternative mine plans under price, cost and permitting shocks.
ideas.problem: Strategic plans are re-run rarely because each scenario takes weeks of specialist time.
ideas.approach: Pair a schedule optimizer with an LLM orchestrator that proposes scenarios, runs them, and explains which assumptions break the plan.
ideas.evidence: Not verified. Operational AI agents are widely marketed, but I did not find an open, auditable approach for strategic scheduling.
ideas.start: Automate three scenarios on a small open-pit schedule.

ideas.title: Haul Roads Mapped from Truck Telemetry
ideas.summary: Estimate rolling resistance and road condition from data trucks already record.
ideas.problem: Poor roads waste fuel and tyres, but inspection is manual and sparse.
ideas.approach: Infer resistance from payload, speed and fuel signals, map it along each route, and trigger grading where it is worst.
ideas.start: Take one month of fleet telemetry and compare fuel burn on one road segment over time.

ideas.title: Dilution Forensics
ideas.summary: Trace each unit of ore dilution back to its probable cause.
ideas.problem: Dilution is measured but rarely attributed, so fixes often target the wrong stage.
ideas.approach: Link drilling, blasting, loading and survey data, and model which factor best explains each dilution event.
ideas.evidence: Not verified. Sensor systems for blast characterisation exist (for example Imdex BLASTDOG), but attributing causes is a separate question.
ideas.start: Pick 50 benches with known dilution and test which logged factors predict it.

ideas.title: Energy-Aware Fleet Dispatch
ideas.summary: Schedule haulage around electricity prices and renewable supply.
ideas.problem: Electrified fleets and on-site solar make energy cost and supply vary by the hour, but dispatch rules ignore it.
ideas.approach: Add energy price and battery state to the dispatch optimizer, and learn supply forecasts.
ideas.start: Simulate a small electric fleet with hourly price data.

ideas.title: Federated Learning for Metallurgical Plants
ideas.summary: Let plants learn from each other's process data without sharing it.
ideas.problem: Plants treat similar ores but guard their data, so each model learns from limited history.
ideas.approach: Train shared models with federated learning, handling very different ores and sensors across sites.
ideas.evidence: Federated learning has been tested for underground mine safety (FedMining, December 2025) and for chemical plants (2026). I found nothing for mineral processing.
ideas.start: Simulate three plants with different ore types and compare local-only and federated models.

ideas.title: Recycled Process Water Twin
ideas.summary: Predict how impurities in recycled water will change flotation or leaching performance.
ideas.problem: As water use is cut, dissolved species build up and degrade recovery in ways operators discover late.
ideas.approach: Combine water-chemistry assays with process data to forecast the impact and recommend bleed or treatment.
ideas.start: Correlate water assays with recovery at a single plant.

ideas.title: Bridging Column Tests and Heap Data
ideas.summary: Learn how lab column results translate into full-scale heap performance.
ideas.problem: Models are mostly fitted on lab tests, but heaps behave differently at scale.
ideas.approach: Use transfer learning with uncertainty to adjust lab-based predictions using heap monitoring data.
ideas.evidence: Reviews describe mostly lab-scale machine learning for leaching. I did not confirm industrial transfer work.
ideas.start: Compare column and heap recovery curves from one operation.

categories.title: Tailings, Water & Closure
categories.description: Managing waste, water and the end of mine life.

ideas.title: Closure Success Forecasting
ideas.summary: Predict years ahead whether a rehabilitated site will recover ecologically, not just turn green.
ideas.problem: Greening indices can mislead. A 2026 study found only 41.8% of mine-affected pixels followed vegetated recovery paths.
ideas.approach: Combine satellite time series with soil and landform data to forecast recovery trajectories and flag likely failures early.
ideas.evidence: Remote-sensing monitoring is established, but a mine-rehabilitation study notes that no appropriate model predicts rehabilitation, and 2026 work calls full recovery assessments rare.
ideas.start: Use public Landsat history for one closed mine and test whether the first three years predict year ten.

ideas.title: Tailings as Ore Maps
ideas.summary: Map critical metals inside legacy tailings the way resource geologists map orebodies.
ideas.problem: Tailings are sampled sparsely, so their metal content and variability are poorly known.
ideas.approach: Combine sparse samples, deposition history and processing records in a spatial model that outputs grade with uncertainty.
ideas.evidence: Geoscience Australia notes the by-product potential of mine waste, while AI work on tailings centres on stability monitoring (for example a 2026 TU Delft research post).
ideas.start: Model a single tailings dam using historic assays by deposition year.

sources.label: TU Delft, tailings monitoring and AI

ideas.title: Long-Horizon Acid Drainage Forecasting
ideas.summary: Forecast water quality decades after closure with physics-informed machine learning.
ideas.problem: Acid and metal-laden drainage can appear long after mining ends.
ideas.approach: Blend geochemical models with monitoring data to forecast with quantified uncertainty.
ideas.start: Fit a simple model to ten years of monitoring data at one site.

ideas.title: Companion-Metal Deportment Tracker
ideas.summary: Follow gallium, germanium and indium through the plant to find where they are lost.
ideas.problem: Companion metals are rarely measured, so their recoverable amount is unknown.
ideas.approach: Predict their concentration in each plant stream from ore chemistry and mineralogy, then rank the cheapest recovery points.
ideas.evidence: Geoscience Australia is estimating in-situ gallium, germanium and indium in zinc deposits with random forests, and notes about half of Australia's critical minerals are co-products. I found no stream-level tracking.
ideas.start: Combine published sphalerite chemistry with a plant mass balance.

ideas.title: Permitting-Time Forecasting
ideas.summary: Forecast how long a project will take to permit.
ideas.problem: Permit delays can erode project value, but timelines are usually guessed.
ideas.approach: Learn from past permit records and documents to give a time range with its drivers.
ideas.start: Collect public permit timelines for one jurisdiction.

ideas.title: Penalty-Element Early Warning
ideas.summary: Predict contaminants in concentrate before shipment.
ideas.problem: Elements such as arsenic raise smelter penalties and can block sales.
ideas.approach: Predict them from ore chemistry and plant data, and suggest blending to stay under limits.
ideas.start: Compare historical shipment assays with upstream ore data.
